Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

royal adjective

also regal, kingly, of the king, the king’s, royal family, royalty

classical

Cic. Rep. 1.50: quīcumque genere rēgiō nātus esset
Cic. Rep. 2.31: īnsignia (Lewis & Short)

rēgius, rēgia, rēgium

declension

royal, of or belonging to a king

The plain word for what belongs to a king: his power, his army, his family (genus rēgium). As a noun, rēgia f. is the palace (Verg. A. 8.363).

Other words

  • rēgālis, rēgāle — kingly, regal, worthy of a king

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.41: genus cīvitātis (Lewis & Short); Ov. M. 1.171: domus (Lewis & Short)

    Like a king, fit for a king: quiddam praestāns et rēgāle (Cic. Rep. 1.69); in Cicero chiefly of monarchy as a form of state, in the poets of royal things.

Examples

  • cum esset habendus rēx, quīcumque genere rēgiō nātus esset

    when anyone born of the royal line had to be accepted as kingCic. Rep. 1.50

  • strātīque vōtīs offerunt tūs, myrrham et aurum rēgium

    and kneeling in prayer they offer frankincense, myrrh and royal goldPrud. Cath. 12.63–64

See also king, queen, prince, princess.
